h2: Pipeline metal loss inspection in Los Angeles: in-line inspection, dig verification and California regulators
html:
Pipeline metal loss inspection in Los Angeles: in-line inspection, dig verification and California regulators

The search that brings most people to this page is "pipeline metal loss inspection services". On a piggable line, metal loss is normally found by an in-line inspection (ILI) tool, usually magnetic flux leakage or ultrasonic, that a specialist ILI vendor runs through the pipe for the operator. Atlantis does not run in-line inspection tools and is not an ILI company. What Atlantis does is the conventional NDT that follows a tool run: it measures and documents the features at the excavations the operator selects, and it examines above-ground piping at stations and terminals with UT, MT, PT and VT.

In-line inspection and dig verification: two halves of one job

An ILI report lists anomalies by log distance, clock position, length, width and estimated depth. The operator's integrity engineers decide which to excavate, either to repair them or to check how accurate the tool was. At the dig, the NDT crew turns an estimate into a measurement. Typical dig work includes:

  • locating the feature from the nearest girth welds and reference markers named in the ILI report
  • a visual record of coating condition and external corrosion before and after cleaning
  • a UT thickness grid across and around the corroded area, plus pit depth readings with a gauge where the external profile can be measured directly; see ultrasonic testing for pipelines
  • magnetic particle testing, often wet fluorescent, to look for stress corrosion cracking under disbonded coating and cracking at dents or weld toes: magnetic particle testing for pipelines
  • UT lamination checks on the pipe body where a sleeve or a weld is planned

The measured profile goes to the operator's engineer, who runs the remaining-strength assessment, for example with ASME B31G or RSTRENG, and decides on repair. Atlantis reports the measurements and does not make that call.

Who regulates Los Angeles pipelines?

California splits pipeline safety by commodity. The Office of the State Fire Marshal's Pipeline Safety Division holds safety authority over intrastate hazardous liquid pipelines, including lines in offshore state waters, under certification from PHMSA, and it monitors operators' hydrostatic tests and in-line inspections. The California Public Utilities Commission's Gas Safety and Reliability Branch covers intrastate gas systems. Pipelines that cross state lines or start in federal waters stay with PHMSA. The integrity management rules behind most dig programs sit in 49 CFR Part 192, Subpart O for gas transmission and 49 CFR 195.452 for hazardous liquid lines.

What a dig verification report should contain

  • the ILI feature number, log distance and girth weld references, so the field result can be matched to the tool call
  • a sketch or photograph with the reading grid laid out from a fixed datum
  • nominal wall, the deepest reading and the axial and circumferential extent of the corroded area
  • MT results with indication location, length and orientation, including a clear statement when none were found
  • procedure revision, technician certification and instrument calibration for each method

How Los Angeles providers compare

ILI vendors sell the tool run and the data analysis. Large integrity firms add engineering, GIS and repair management. Field NDT firms supply crews for digs and station piping. When you compare bids for dig work, ask whether the crew will report a measured profile you can use for the remaining-strength calculation, whether MT technicians are certified for the technique you specify, and when the report will be issued. Get the answer to the last one in writing.

Atlantis on Los Angeles pipeline work

Atlantis is based in Houston and sends crews to Los Angeles digs, pump stations and terminal piping for agreed dates, working under procedures approved by an ASNT NDT Level III. New girth welds that need radiographs go to a licensed radiography contractor, since Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States; the Level III can review those images on request.
